claims.statement: All backend HTTP routers are mounted under a single `APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1")` in `src/main.py` (account, portfolio, auth, institutions, integration, market, and the service-token market `data_router`), while the WebSocket and worker-dashboard routers are mounted outside that prefix; the frontend `apiClient` hard-codes the same `/api/v1` base.

Editing a backend model requires a matching Alembic revision shipped in the same change, and every migration file MUST follow the `<hash>_<description>.py` naming convention under `migrations/versions/` (`alembic.ini` sets `script_location = migrations`); manual SQL migrations are created via autogenerate and use `op.execute()` inside a standard revision, and `src/main.py` upgrades the database to `head` at startup except when `settings.environment == "test"`.

The `AccountModel` table `accounts` is unique on `(user_id, institution_id, external_id)`, carries `api_sync_enabled`, `net_deposits`, `free_cash` (default `0.0`), `broker_value`/`broker_value_at`, `last_sync_at` and a nullable `integration_user_id` foreign key to `integration_users.id`, and cascades `all, delete-orphan` to its positions and portfolio associations.

`InstitutionModel.csv_format` is a comma-separated positional template string using standardized `{placeholder}` tokens that maps each column of a broker CSV export in order; `csv_import_enabled` plus a non-null `csv_format` is the gate that enables CSV import for an institution, and `src/commands/seed.py` documents the worked Wealthsimple example.

`GenericCsvParser` is template-driven: it normalizes template and header tokens to lowercase snake_case and validates the header count and each column against alias sets, raising a specific `CsvParserError` subclass on mismatch; `is_cash_row` returns `False` for equity-like security types and `True` for a blank symbol, a `cash`/`currency` security type, a `cash`/`cad`/`usd` symbol or a `sec-c-*` symbol, cash rows accumulate into the discovered account's `free_cash` instead of becoming positions, option rows (OCC-style symbols, `option`/`derivative` types) are dropped, and `average_cost` is `book_value / quantity` quantized to 4 decimals or `None` when quantity is non-positive or book value is missing.

`PositionRepository.sync_by_account` implements position sync as a full replace: it deletes every `PositionModel` row for the account and re-inserts the supplied positions, so partial syncs cannot leave stale holdings.

`PositionService.sync_account_positions` is a no-op when the account has no `integration_user_id`, raises `ApiSyncDisabledError` when `api_sync_enabled` is false, and otherwise enqueues the broker sync via `IntegrationAccountApi`; `POST /accounts/{account_id}/sync` pre-checks the same flag and is rate-limited to 3 requests per minute.

Account holdings and totals convert every position value from the security/position currency into the account currency with `stockholm.Money` and the `CurrencyConverter` obtained from `FxRateProvider`; `_account_performance` derives P/L against an explicit `ProfitLossBasis` — `net_deposits` when they are set, otherwise the positions cost basis — folds converted `free_cash` into both cost and value, reports `return_percent` as `None` when the denominator is zero, and counts unpriced positions into `unpriced_positions`/`pricing_incomplete`; holding rows additionally carry `display_total_value`/`display_currency` so cross-currency rows can be aggregated without adding unlike currencies.

The account router exposes per-user chart preferences at `GET|PUT|PATCH /accounts/me/preferences`, backed by `UserApi.get_preferences`/`save_preferences`/`patch_preferences` on the `auth_users.preferences` JSON column: GET returns `{}` when nothing is saved, PUT replaces the document with `model_dump(exclude_none=True)` so explicit null fields are dropped, and PATCH merges through a JSONB `||` update that returns the merged document; the per-key read/write matrix lives in the User Preferences concept page.

`POST /accounts/csv/inspect` and `POST /accounts/csv/import` accept `institution_id` either as a multipart form field or as a query parameter with the same alias, `csv/import` additionally accepts `account_numbers` and `currencies` the same way, and both `csv/import` and `POST /accounts/{account_id}/csv-sync` accept `net_deposits`; account numbers may be a JSON list string, a comma-separated string, or repeated values (normalized and deduplicated in order), missing `institution_id` or `account_numbers` yields HTTP 422, and `net_deposits` is parsed strictly as a `{account_number: number | null}` JSON object — malformed JSON, a non-object or a non-numeric value is a 422 rather than a silent drop.

`CsvAccountService.inspect_csv` marks discovered accounts the user already has for that institution (`exists = True` plus the stored currency and `net_deposits`), and `import_accounts` creates new accounts with `api_sync_enabled=False` and the parsed `free_cash` or refreshes existing ones by updating currency/`free_cash`/`net_deposits` and re-syncing positions, resolving each holding through `SecurityApi.get_or_create_from_broker` and wrapping resolution failures in `SecurityResolutionError`; `sync_account_from_csv` updates `free_cash`, an optional `net_deposits` and the positions of one stored account.

The auth domain persists five tables — `auth_users` (unique indexed email, argon2 `_password_hash`, `is_active`, `is_verified`, `last_login_at`, JSON `preferences`), `auth_verification_tokens`, `auth_totp`, `auth_recovery_codes`, and `auth_passkeys` — and the TOTP, recovery-code, and passkey tables cascade on user deletion.

`UserApi.login` returns a `LoginChallengeResponse` carrying a 5-minute `mfa_pending`-scope JWT instead of an access token when the user has a verified TOTP record; the client completes the challenge at `POST /auth/2fa/login-verify`, which sets the same `auth_token` cookie as password login.

`AuthorizationApi.check_entity_owned_by_user` raises HTTP 404 rather than 403 when the entity is missing or not owned by the user, deliberately hiding entity existence; `src/main.py` maps `AuthorizationError` and `EntityNotFoundError` to 404 responses with an `{"error": ...}` body.

`SecurityModel` is unique on `(symbol, exchange)` (allowing the same ticker on different venues) and `SecurityBrokerModel` records the broker to security mapping (institution, broker symbol/exchange, mapped symbol/exchange, `search_results` JSON) indexed on `(institution_id, broker_symbol, broker_exchange)`.

Price-related market tables are `market_prices` (unique `(security_id, date)`, OHLC plus `adjusted_close` as `DECIMAL(16,8)`) and `market_intraday_prices` (unique `(security_id, timestamp)`, 1-hour candles), and per-user market tables are keyed by `user_id` for watchlists, price alerts, security notes, security documents, and chart snapshots — with `market_chart_snapshots` indexed on `(security_id, user_id, captured_at)`.

`SecurityApi.get_or_create_from_broker` first checks the broker mapping table, then maps the broker symbol (`.` to `-`) and exchange (`CSE` to `CA`, `TSX` to `TO`, `NYSE` to `US`, `NASDAQ` to `US`), searches EODHD (through `SecuritySearchCache` when present), takes the first result, warms prices via `MarketPricesApi.get_latest_close`, and persists the mapping with the raw search results; zero search results raise `ValueError`.

`EodhdPriceRepository` is the registered `PriceRepository` implementation and adds read-through caching: `get_prices` merges stored rows with fresh EODHD rows (EODHD winning per date) and persists the union, `get_latest_price` only refetches when the stored close predates the last NYSE trading day (computed with `holidays.NYSE()`), and `save_price`/`save_prices` deliberately raise `NotImplementedError` so writes go through the inner SQLAlchemy repository; its factory builds the EODHD gateway directly rather than resolving the `MarketGateway` svcs key.

`GET /market/prices/{security_id}` supports `interval` in `1d|1w|1m|1h|4h`: daily/weekly/monthly require both `from_date` and `to_date` (HTTP 422 otherwise) and aggregate in process, while intraday reads `market_intraday_prices` and lazily backfills via `MarketService.fetch_and_save_intraday_prices` when the stored window is stale.

The market router exposes price alerts, security notes, documents, and chart snapshots as per-security sub-resources under `/market/securities/{security_id}/...` (alerts GET/POST/DELETE, notes GET/POST/PUT/DELETE, documents GET/POST/DELETE, snapshots GET/POST 201/DELETE 204); note create and update both enqueue `generate_note_title_task` so the title is regenerated by AI in the worker, and document uploads are written to `settings.upload_path` under a random `uuid4` filename with only metadata persisted.

Indicator endpoints split between `GET /market/securities/{security_id}/indicators`, which computes MAs/MACD/RSI in process and caches results in Redis via `IndicatorCache`, and `POST .../indicators/compute`, which builds or accepts a candle series (aggregating weekly/monthly/4h as needed, optionally applying Heikin-Ashi), validates `from_date <= to_date` (422), and delegates computation to the external Go sidecar through `IndicatorServiceClient`; caller-supplied candles bypass the cache.

The AI endpoints `POST /market/securities/{security_id}/ai/fundamentals`, `/ai/summarize-notes`, and `/ai/portfolio-debate` are each rate-limited to 5 requests per minute and map `TimeoutError` to HTTP 504 and `RuntimeError` to HTTP 503.

`MarketService` updates prices for all active securities — a one-year window daily and a seven-day window of 1-hour intraday candles hourly — pushing blocking gateway I/O through `asyncio.to_thread` and gathering per-security calls with `asyncio.gather`, swallowing per-security exceptions so one failure cannot abort the batch (returning `success`/`failure` counts).

`src/market/task.py` chains the scheduled pipeline: `daily_price_update` runs at midnight, `hourly_intraday_price_update` runs every hour and then enqueues `recalculate_all_account_totals_task` (which sweeps active accounts and pushes `AccountTotalsUpdatedMessage` over the WebSocket manager) and `check_and_dispatch_price_alerts` in isolated try/except blocks, the alert path enqueues a retrying `alert_email_dispatch_task` (`retries=3`) per triggered alert that marks the alert triggered, and `daily_fx_refresh` runs at 17:30 UTC to refresh the ECB rates stored in Redis.

`IntegrationUserModel` (table `integration_users`) is unique on `(user_id, institution_id, external_user_id)`, and `IntegrationAccountApi.sync_account_positions` enqueues `sync_account_positions_task` with the broker gateway class resolved from the account's institution via `get_broker_gateway_class`.

`BrokerApiGateway` declares `login`, `get_accounts`, and `get_positions_by_account`, and its constructor unconditionally installs keyring's `PlaintextKeyring` — flagged with a TODO to secure before staging — so broker session tokens are stored in plaintext on disk.

`_sync_account_positions_task` orchestrates broker sync in the Huey worker: it marks the sync active in Redis, emits `ACCOUNT_SYNC_STARTED`, resolves each broker position to a security via `SecurityApi.get_or_create_from_broker`, replaces positions through `PositionApi.create`, refreshes `free_cash` (only when the gateway overrides `get_cash_balances`), `net_deposits`, `broker_value` and `last_sync_at`, and reconciles the broker value against `PositionService.get_total_for_account` with a 1% warning; it then emits success or a mapped plain-language error email plus `ACCOUNT_SYNC_FAILED`, the Redis marker is always cleared in `finally`, and an interrupted-task signal handler clears it for interrupted tasks.

The integration router exposes `GET /integration/institutions` for enabled institutions and `/external` endpoints for broker users, login (mapping `OTPRequiredError` to 400 `OTP_REQUIRED` and `LoginFailedError` to 401 `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`), account listing, `POST /external/accounts/import` (3/minute, deduplicating via `AccountApi.import_from_broker` and enqueuing one sync task per newly created account), and `POST /external/positions/import` for synchronous single-account import; every route touching an `IntegrationUser` first calls `check_entity_owned_by_user`.

`ConnectionManager` tracks per-user WebSocket connections and fans out messages by publishing a user_id and message payload to Redis Pub/Sub channel `ws_messages`, keeping one Redis client per running event loop and falling back to local delivery when publishing fails; `/api/ws` authenticates via a signed single-use ticket (verified with `max_age=30`, salt `ws-ticket`, replay-guarded by a Redis key with 30 s expiry) or the `auth_token` cookie / `sec-websocket-protocol` header, closing with 1008 on failure.

`src/core/exception.py` defines the two abstract base exceptions every domain error derives from — `EntityNotFoundError` (with `entity_id`/`entity_name`) and `AuthorizationError` (requiring `log_message()`) — and `src/main.py` maps both to HTTP 404 with an error body.

`src/core/pagination.py` defines `PaginationParams` (`offset >= 0`, `1 <= limit <= 100`, default 50) and the generic `PaginatedResponse` wrapper, which is the response shape used by account holdings, watchlist securities, alerts, and notes endpoints.

`register_services` in `src/config/services.py` binds `AsyncSession` to the session manager, registers core/account/auth services unconditionally, and then branches on `settings.stub_external_api` to register either live or stub integration and market services.

Each domain exposes its own `register_*_services(registry)` function (for example `register_account_services` and `register_market_services`) that registers repositories, APIs, and services as `svcs` factories, so nothing is constructed by hand in a handler.

Extending the backend requires: for a new domain, following the layered file set and calling `register_services` plus including the router in the `/api/v1` router in `src/main.py`; for a new broker, adding an `InstitutionEnum` value, seeding it, implementing `BrokerApiGateway` (overriding `get_cash_balances` only when the broker reports cash), and wiring `get_broker_gateway_class`; and for a new market provider, implementing `MarketGateway` and choosing the registration key — repointing `MarketGateway` for a drop-in replacement of the EODHD flows, or `DataPlaneMarketGateway` for the provider-agnostic data plane — in both the live and the stub registration.

Tests must not depend on external services — Redis is globally faked, HTTP/broker/SMTP clients are stubbed or patched, and only the ephemeral testcontainers PostgreSQL is allowed — and the backend test suite is grouped into `tests/routers/`, `tests/services/`, per-domain folders such as `tests/account/` and `tests/market/`, `tests/integration/brokers/`, and `tests/ws/`.

The market router's watchlist surface is `GET|POST /market/watchlists` (POST 201), `PATCH /market/watchlists/{watchlist_id}` (rename and/or sort mode), `DELETE /market/watchlists/{watchlist_id}` (204), `GET /market/watchlists/{watchlist_id}/securities` (paginated `PaginatedResponse[SecuritySchema]`), `POST|DELETE /market/watchlists/{watchlist_id}/securities/{security_id}`, `PUT /market/watchlists/{watchlist_id}/securities/order` (manual-order replacement), and the default-watchlist shortcuts `POST|DELETE /market/watchlists/securities/{security_id}`; every route requires `current_user`, and each mutation returns the updated `WatchlistRead` with its securities embedded.

`WatchlistRepository` (`src/market/repository.py`) is the contract the market router uses directly for watchlists — there is no watchlist service — and declares `get_by_user`, `create`, `rename`, `update_sort`, `set_security_order`, `delete`, `create_default`, the default-watchlist shortcuts `add_security`/`remove_security`, the per-watchlist `add_security_to_watchlist`/`remove_security_from_watchlist`, and the paged `get_securities`; the ABC requires every implementation to scope operations to the owning `user_id` and to report a watchlist that is missing *or* owned by another user as `WatchlistNotFoundError` so callers cannot distinguish the two.

`SqlAlchemyWatchlistRepository` converts the `(user_id, name)` unique violation into `WatchlistDuplicateNameError` after a rollback on both create and rename, resolves the default watchlist by the literal name `"Default"` (creating it on the first `add_security`, tolerating a concurrent-create `IntegrityError` by re-reading, and raising `WatchlistNotFoundError` for the nil UUID from `remove_security` when absent), raises `SecurityNotFoundError` for an unknown security in membership edits, treats removing a non-member as a no-op, appends a new membership at `max(position) + 1` (documented as not concurrency-safe, which is acceptable for single-user watchlists), and returns every `WatchlistRead` with `sort` plus `WatchlistSecuritySchema` members ordered by `position` and price-enriched with `current_price`, `daily_price_change`, and `daily_price_change_percent` from one batched query over the latest two closes per security.

`WatchlistDuplicateNameError` deliberately extends plain `Exception` rather than `EntityNotFoundError`, so the global `EntityNotFoundError` handler does not turn it into a 404 and the watchlist routes translate it to HTTP 409.

Every market table that references a security holds a real foreign key to `market_securities.id` (`market_securities_broker`, `market_prices`, `market_intraday_prices`, `market_watchlists_securities`, `market_price_alerts`, `market_security_notes`, `market_security_documents`, `market_chart_snapshots`); the only cross-domain `security_id` column without a database-level foreign key is `account_positions.security_id` in the account domain.

The layering rules this page owns are: models generate migrations and are never returned to clients (routes return `*Read` schemas), repositories and services exchange schemas rather than ORM models, `api_types.py` is the only type surface that may cross a domain boundary, and a router may call its own domain's repositories directly for thin CRUD routes — as the market watchlist routes do — but must never touch a foreign domain's repositories.

`market_watchlists_securities` is an association entity rather than a bare join table: it carries a server-defaulted `added_at` and an application-managed `position`, while `market_watchlists` carries a persisted `sort` mode defaulting to `custom`; because a SQLAlchemy `secondary` relationship can neither carry nor order by those association columns, the watchlist read paths query the association explicitly, joined to the security rows and ordered by `position` then `added_at`.

`PUT /market/watchlists/{watchlist_id}/securities/order` replaces a watchlist's manual ordering: the payload must be an exact permutation of the current membership (a repeated id is rejected by the length check), validation runs before any write so a rejected payload leaves every position untouched, and a rejected payload raises `WatchlistOrderIdentityError` — deliberately a plain `Exception`, not an `EntityNotFoundError` — which the route translates to HTTP 422.

`PATCH /market/watchlists/{watchlist_id}` renames and/or changes the sort mode in one call and translates `WatchlistDuplicateNameError` to HTTP 409; a payload that changes nothing still proves ownership by re-reading the user's watchlists and raising `WatchlistNotFoundError` when the id is absent, so a no-op PATCH cannot be used to probe another user's watchlist.

`src/market/enum.py` owns the watchlist sort modes (`custom`, `name_asc`, `price_change_desc`, `price_change_asc`, `date_added`, `date_added_asc`) and the candle intervals (`1h`, `4h`, `1d`, `1w`, `1m`); the watchlist repository persists whatever sort value it is given but never orders by it, and `get_securities` pages a `symbol`-ordered subset, so display sort is applied above the repository rather than in SQL.

`migrations/versions/4c2ed77e7738_add_watchlist_sort_membership_added_at_.py` is the worked example of the mandatory model-change-plus-migration rule: it adds `market_watchlists.sort` and `market_watchlists_securities.added_at`/`position`, backfills existing rows deterministically (`row_number()` partitioned by watchlist ordered by `security_id`), and only then enforces `NOT NULL`.

The account router exposes three holdings reads — `GET /accounts/holdings` (paginated `UserHoldingRead` aggregated across every account the user owns), `GET /accounts/holdings/{security_id}` (security-scoped), and `GET /accounts/{account_id}/holdings` (account-scoped, with header totals computed over all positions) — each passing a display currency into `PositionService` (the user's stored preference for the user-wide read, the account currency otherwise); `PositionService.get_holdings_by_security` returns an empty list with a zero total when the security itself cannot be resolved (a TODO flags the ambiguity with "no holdings"), while `_calculate_holdings` logs and skips an unresolvable position and returns a position without a stored price as a zero-value row excluded from the totals.

`CsvAccountService.validate_csv_institution` is the single gate for CSV import: an unknown institution raises `InstitutionNotFoundError`, and an institution with `csv_import_enabled` false or a null `csv_format` raises `CsvImportDisabledError`, so enabling CSV support for a broker is a data change (template plus flag) rather than a parser change.

`ws_manager` (`src/ws/manager.py`) is the single fan-out the account-totals task and the integration broker-sync task push through, so realtime account updates originate in the Huey worker processes rather than in the API process.

The market domain owns a per-user security valuation entity: `SecurityValuationModel` in `market_security_valuations` keyed by integer id with `user_id`, a cascading `security_id` foreign key to `market_securities.id`, `lower_bound`/`upper_bound` as `DECIMAL(16,8)`, and `created_at`/`updated_at`, constrained unique on `(user_id, security_id)` as `valuation_user_security_unique` and indexed by `ix_market_security_valuations_user_security`; it shipped in `migrations/versions/3436586a755f_create_security_valuations.py`.

`SecurityValuationRepository` is a market repository contract the router uses directly with no service layer between them, declaring `get_by_security_and_user`, `upsert`, `get_history`, and `get_batch_by_user_and_securities`; `SqlAlchemySecurityValuationRepository` scopes every read and write to `user_id`, returns `[]` for an empty batch id list, and its `upsert` updates the existing `(user_id, security_id)` row or inserts a new one, appends a `SecurityValuationHistoryModel` revision row in **both** branches, then commits and refreshes before returning.

The market router exposes the valuation surface as `GET /market/securities/{security_id}/valuation` (404 when the user has no valuation), `PUT /market/securities/{security_id}/valuation` (upsert from `SecurityValuationWrite`, which carries only `lower_bound`/`upper_bound`), and both `GET` (repeated `security_ids` query params) and `POST` (`SecurityValuationBatchRequest` body) forms of `/market/securities/valuation/batch`; the batch routes are declared before the `{security_id}` routes so the literal path is not captured as a security id, and `SecurityValuationRead` echoes `id`, `user_id`, `security_id`, both bounds and both timestamps while `SecurityValuationHistoryRead` omits `updated_at`.

`SecurityValuationRepository` is registered as a factory in both the live `register_market_services` (`src/market/__init__.py`) and the stub market registration in `src/config/services.py`, so the valuation routes resolve the same repository implementation regardless of `settings.stub_external_api`.

`SecurityValuationHistoryModel` maps to `market_security_valuation_history` with an integer `id`, `user_id`, a cascading `security_id` foreign key to `market_securities.id`, `lower_bound`/`upper_bound` as `DECIMAL(16,8)`, and `created_at`, indexed by `ix_market_security_valuation_history_user_security_created` on `(user_id, security_id, created_at)` and carrying **no** unique constraint, so it stores one row per valuation write; the table shipped in `migrations/versions/b291707f24ca_add_market_security_valuation_history.py`, later than the current-value table.

`market_security_valuation_history` is a revision log rather than a child of `market_security_valuations`: it declares no foreign key to the current-value table and is correlated to it only by the shared `(user_id, security_id)` pair, so deleting a security cascades away both its current range and its entire revision history, the current-value table stays bounded at one row per pair through `valuation_user_security_unique`, and the history table grows one row per write.

`SqlAlchemySecurityValuationRepository.get_history(security_id, user_id)` returns every revision row for that pair ordered by `created_at` then `id` ascending as `SecurityValuationHistoryRead`, scoped to `user_id`, but no route exposes it — the valuation HTTP surface is read-current plus upsert only — so the revision log is currently reachable only from code that resolves the repository itself.

`tests/market/test_security_valuation_repository.py` pins the valuation repository's observable behaviour: a second upsert for the same `(user, security)` keeps the original row id with new bounds, an empty batch id list returns `[]` while a batch read excludes another user's rows for the same security, and two upserts for one pair yield exactly two history rows in ascending `created_at` order.

The router-only repository recipe requires the repository itself to carry the ownership and error rules a service would otherwise hold: the `WatchlistRepository` ABC documents that implementations must scope every operation to the owning `user_id` and report a resource that is missing *or* owned by another user as the domain's `EntityNotFoundError` subclass (which the global handler maps to HTTP 404), while errors a route must translate to a different status — `WatchlistDuplicateNameError` and `WatchlistOrderIdentityError` — deliberately extend plain `Exception` so the global handler does not claim them.

The market domain exposes two serving surfaces that differ by authentication rather than by feature area: `market_router` (`/market/...`) requires the user-JWT `current_user` on every route and serves the SPA from the domain repositories, while `data_router` (`/market/data/...`) is guarded by `require_service_token` — a shared secret read only from the `X-Service-Token` header and compared with `secrets.compare_digest`, with no cookie fallback — and serves trusted services such as the Go MCP gateway.

`DataPlaneMarketGateway` is a behaviour-free subclass of `MarketGateway` that exists solely as a distinct svcs registration key: the legacy `MarketGateway` binding stays on EODHD (`eodhd_gateway_factory`) for the existing price flows, while `DataPlaneMarketGateway` resolves `composite_market_gateway_factory` — the composed FMP/Polygon gateway that routes prices, search, symbol lookup and fundamentals to FMP and options to Polygon and releases both provider HTTP clients on container teardown — and both keys are registered identically in the live and stub market registrations.
The FastAPI lifespan resolves `DataPlaneMarketGateway` eagerly during startup, so a missing provider key or a broken gateway registration fails at boot instead of on the first data-plane request.

`EndpointResponseCache` (`src/market/endpoint_cache.py`) is the single canonical cache for the service-to-service data endpoints, storing responses under the `market:ep` prefix keyed by data class, endpoint and a canonical hash of the request parameters; per-data-class TTLs come from the `endpoint_ttl_*` settings and are read at call time, a provider-reported miss is negative-cached for `endpoint_ttl_negative_seconds` so a repeated lookup returns the same 404 instead of burning upstream quota, and any Redis failure degrades to a live fetch rather than propagating.

`data_router` exposes eight service-token GET routes under `/api/v1/market/data` (`prices/{symbol}`, `quote/{symbol}`, `indicators/{symbol}`, `symbols/search`, `options/{symbol}`, `options/{symbol}/expirations`, `fundamentals/{symbol}`, `fundamentals/{symbol}/statements`); the paths and query parameter names are a frozen contract for the MCP gateway, pinned by the committed OpenAPI artifact `tests/market/contracts/data_plane_openapi.json`, which must match the live FastAPI schema byte-for-byte and cover exactly those routes.

`GET /market/securities/{security_id}/institutional-ownership` is a user route that reads through the data-plane gateway: it resolves the security from the repository first (unknown id becomes 404), calls `DataPlaneMarketGateway.get_institutional_ownership` on a thread, and caches the JSON payload in Redis for 24 h under `market:institutional_ownership:{security_id}`; both a `MarketDataNotFoundError` and a `MarketDataProviderError` degrade to an empty payload (null metrics, empty history) with the symbol echoed back, and only the provider error skips the cache write.

`data_router` maps provider failures itself rather than in the gateway: `MarketDataNotFoundError` becomes 404, `MarketDataConfigurationError` 503, and any other provider failure 502, always with a generic detail string that never names the provider; `MarketGateway`'s non-price capabilities (symbol lookup, fundamentals, options, quotes, institutional ownership) are deliberately non-abstract, defaulting to `MarketDataProviderError("capability not supported by this provider")` so the EODHD gateway stays concrete and instantiable while the composite overrides what FMP/Polygon can serve.

Broker sync refreshes cash and broker-reported value as account attributes: `_do_sync_positions` calls `AccountApi.update_free_cash` only when the gateway overrides the non-abstract `BrokerApiGateway.get_cash_balances` (converting and summing the per-currency balances into the account currency), calls `AccountApi.update_broker_value`, and `_reconcile_broker_value` logs a warning when the broker value and `PositionService.get_total_for_account` differ by more than 1% of the broker value.

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` accepts an optional `currency` query parameter validated against `SUPPORTED_DISPLAY_CURRENCIES` (`CAD`, `USD`, `EUR`, `GBP`, 422 otherwise) and defaults to the account's own currency, while the holdings routes pass the user's stored `display_currency` preference (default `CAD`) into `PositionService`, so cross-currency holding rows expose `display_total_value`/`display_currency` alongside the native `total_value`.

`FxRateProvider` (`src/market/fx.py`) builds its `CurrencyConverter` from a daily ECB snapshot stored in Redis under `fx:ecb:zip`/`fx:ecb:fetched_at` by the `daily_fx_refresh` Huey task, caches the parsed converter per fetch date at module level (providers are request-scoped), warns when the freshest rate is more than three business days old, and falls back to the package's bundled snapshot when Redis is empty or unreachable; `PositionService` obtains its converter from this provider instead of constructing `CurrencyConverter()` itself.

`repository_*.py` denotes an alternative backend implementation of a domain's repository contract rather than a second implementation to keep in sync: the ABC lives in `repository.py`, the default SQLAlchemy implementation in `repository_sqlalchemy.py`, and a `repository_<impl>.py` (for example `repository_eodhd.py`) may be registered in its place behind the same interface — decorating the SQLAlchemy implementation while raising `NotImplementedError` for writes it does not own — so it must be swappable through the svcs registry alone.
